title: Fast assembly and in vivo coalescence of ParBF biocondensates involved in bacterial DNA partition.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Pulled the open-access full text and its data availability statement; searched the whole text for accessions, repository links, code links and supplementary item names (only Supplementary Table S1 = strains/plasmids and S2 = oligonucleotides are referenced). Zenodo/Dryad DOI search returned nothing; NCBI links returned only the PMC record; Europe PMC's supplementary-file endpoint failed (HTTP 500, then two read timeouts), so no supplementary file was opened.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: All measurement counts (144-411 cells per skewness condition, 50 fusion events, N = 807/283/120/86 cells for mobility, N = 660 and N = 60 for critical surface tension, >1700 and 1150 cells for hexanediol time courses) come from the figure legends and results text, not from any file. The existence and contents of Supplementary Tables S1-S2 are also text-only.

a1_downloadable.note: The data availability statement says only: 'All data generated or analyzed during this study are included in this published article and its supplementary information files.' No repository accession, no source-data file, no deposited microscopy images (no BioImage Archive/IDR/Zenodo entry found), and the only named supplementary tables hold bacterial strains and DNA primers. The numbers a model would need exist as plotted points in figures.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Every candidate label (does a pair of ParB protein clusters fuse on contact, fusion time, diffusion coefficient, fluorescence skewness) is a quantity the authors computed from time-lapse microscopy movies in ImageJ/MicrobeJ/TrackMate. Those movies and the per-cell measurement tables are not released, so the label would have to be re-constructed from images we cannot obtain.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs would be the fluorescence image stacks or per-track coordinates; neither is deposited. Only protein variant names (e.g. ParB-R156A) and strain descriptions are available.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated clearly in the text (micronewtons per metre for surface tension, seconds, micrometres squared per second), but only for summary values in figures.

a5_enough_rows.note: The largest reported unit counts are a few thousand segmented cells for skewness and only 50 fusion events for the key fusion measurement - and none of it is in a file to count. No row count verified.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: unknown; released supplement appears to be PDF/Word tables plus movies
a6_fits_laptop.note: Nothing large exists to download, so size is not the problem.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked at all: there is no download to compare against the paper's counts.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels would be genuine physical measurements (fluorescence intensity, position over time), not another model's output - this is the one killer the paper would pass if the data existed.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model) would fit ParB sequence variants; Cellpose/DeepBacs-style segmentation networks would fit the images
backbone.hardware: CPU would suffice for the handful of protein variants, but there are far too few labelled examples
backbone.licence: ESM-2 is MIT-licensed; irrelevant here because no training data is available

integration.partner_dataset: UniProt / AlphaFold DB for ParB family sequences and structures (join on UniProt accession); PhaSepDB or similar condensate databases
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Which features of a DNA-binding protein's sequence decide whether its clusters fuse on contact rather than staying separate? - a good question, but this paper contributes no joinable per-item measurements to answer it.

controls.positive_control: The paper's own mutant contrast would serve (wild-type ParB gives skewness ~1.85 versus ~0.70-0.72 for the assembly-defective R156A variant and the parA deletion), if the per-cell values were released.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling would be trivial to run - but there are no labels to shuffle.
controls.external_validation: Other ParB imaging studies (e.g. Caulobacter, Bacillus ParB) exist in the literature, but their per-cell measurements are likewise locked in figures.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: without the per-cell or per-track measurements, no model can be trained or evaluated on this study's data at all.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use live-cell images of bacterial protein droplets to predict whether two droplets will merge when they touch.
plain_idea.train_on: Would need time-lapse fluorescence microscopy of Escherichia coli cells carrying F plasmids, with each example a pair of ParB protein clusters approaching each other; the paper reports only 50 scored fusion events and none of the underlying data is released.
plain_idea.predict: Whether an encounter ends in fusion, and how fast - the truth coming from manual/semi-automated scoring of the movies by the authors, which was never deposited.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Bacterial geneticists studying plasmid inheritance would learn which physical parameters set the fusion-versus-separation boundary; as it stands nothing can be learned because the measurements are only visible as dots in published figures.

ml_idea: Considered: predict fusion-versus-no-fusion (and fusion kinetics) for encountering ParB condensates from image features, or predict condensate assembly competence from ParB sequence variants. Both die on data availability - the study releases no images, no tracks and no measurement tables, only strain and primer lists.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: there is no dataset to size.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the data availability statement and the list of supplementary items - it took one query to see that the only files are strain and oligonucleotide tables, with all measurements confined to figures.

verdict_reason: A single-lab microscopy study with no deposited data: the availability statement points only to the article and supplementary tables of strains and primers, so the images, tracks and per-cell measurements a model would need do not exist in any downloadable form (A1, A2, A3, A5, A7 all fail). Even the paper's own numbers are small - 50 scored fusion events.
